about: Shared cross-language fixture for OrderRouter. The TypeScript, Python, PHP, C# and Go test suites all read THIS file and assert the same expectations, so an implementation that drifts in one language fails there and only there.
comparison: Numbers are IEEE-754 doubles: compare them with a relative tolerance of 1e-9, never as text. Strings, booleans and array lengths compare exactly. Every field listed under expected must be present in the produced structure.

safetyCases.about: The default is NO CAP. This class does not decide how much of your money you may trade: the same plan that trips a 25 USD cap passes untouched when no cap is set. maxNotionalUsd is an opt-in guardrail, not a ceiling.

The counterpart to missing_rate_blocks_never_skips. A step that cannot be valued in USD BLOCKS when a cap is in force, because a cap that silently disappears is not a cap. With no cap there is nothing to enforce, so the caller is not made to supply usdRates for a check they never asked for.

reconcileSequenceCases.about: Each leg used to compute a scale from the hop total and multiply the downstream amounts by it, so the second leg scaled an already-scaled number: 0.9 x 0.8 = 0.72 of the hop instead of the true 0.70, sizing the next hop at 144 when only 140 had arrived. Over-sizing the next hop is not a rounding nuisance — it is a guaranteed insufficient-funds halt on exactly the bridged routes this class exists for. reconcileExecutionStep is pure and cannot remember across calls, so the hop's cumulative shortfall lives on the steps themselves, written by applyResize; that is why this case can only be expressed as a SEQUENCE. The tolerance is 1 so the shortfalls resize rather than halt.

The combined-scale change must be arithmetically inert when there is nothing to combine, which is every case the rest of this fixture covers: with one leg per hop priorShortfall is 0 and scaleBefore is 1.

mixedHopIndexTypes.about: A plan whose hopIndex is written 0 on one step and 0.0 on the next. THE 0.0 MUST STAY 0.0: it is the whole point of the case. Both are the same number, but json_decode gives PHP an int for one and a float for the other, and PHP's === compares type as well as value — so a hop total built with === silently drops the second leg and resizes every downstream order wrong. Do not regenerate this section by round-tripping the file through a JSON serializer that renders 0.0 as 0.
